title: Plan created minimal test infrastructure instead of comprehensive async test fixtures
description: Plan specified only a 'functional settings fixture' for conftest.py, but a FastAPI + SQLAlchemy async project needs at minimum: async_session fixture (real PostgreSQL, per-test transaction rollback), async_client fixture (httpx.AsyncClient with app dependency overrides), and authenticated_client fixture (mock CurrentUser). Without these, no downstream epic can write integration tests. The plan also deferred test database strategy ('Testcontainers recommended, defer to implementation phase') when it should be a Phase 1 standard.
root_cause: plan_phase_epic treated test infrastructure as a simple fixture replacement task rather than recognizing it as a foundational standard that all downstream epics depend on. It didn't analyze what fixtures downstream epics would need to import.
recommendation: When generating testing standards plans, plan_phase_epic should: (1) analyze downstream epic interfaces_consumed to understand what test fixtures they'll need, (2) define the full fixture hierarchy (settings → database session → HTTP client → authenticated client), (3) NOT defer test database strategy — define it as a standard (PostgreSQL service container in CI, testcontainers for local dev). Also specify pytest-asyncio loop_scope configuration for session-scoped async fixtures.
affected_section: Implementation Approach generation — specifically TECH-4 testing standards and conftest.py scope.
plan_context: Phase 1 Epic 2 — Tech Stack Standards, pytest + FastAPI async testing
